title: Case: Tracking shows a parcel as delivered and the recipient phones to ask what is being done
context: A boxed set of kitchen knives (order TG-4631, shipment DL-9245) scanned as delivered on 2027-03-16. The recipient says it did not arrive. The carrier's Parcel trace team owns delivery traces.
initial_request: Hello, yes, it's Lysander Moorcroft again, I'm ringing because I've written on your portal three times now and all I get back is the automatic thing about one working day and an email this morning telling me my order has been delivered and would I like to review it, which, frankly. I've been in since Tuesday. I've looked in the porch, behind the bins, I've asked both sides. I'm not being funny but those knives were a wedding present for my nephew and the wedding is a week on Saturday. I answered the question about the door yesterday, I wrote it all out, and I've no idea whether anybody read it or whether it's just sitting there. I don't want a survey, I don't want a discount code. Has anyone actually done anything with what I told you? What happens now? Because if it's just gone, somebody needs to say so and send another one.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Tumblewell Arc Logistics
events.body: Trace TR-3107 opened for DL-9245. The delivery photo shows a green front door with a brass number 22 and a boot scraper to the left. We have not sent the photo to the recipient. Before we pull the driver's GPS record we need one thing from her, in her own words: does that description match her front door, yes or no, and if no, what does hers look like. Send her answer to us by email quoting TR-3107. We do not need anything else at this stage.

Someone from the carrier rang and read me a description of a photo and then got cut off before I could answer properly. Green door, brass 22, boot scraper. That is not my house. My door is dark blue, the 22 is white stick-on numbers on the glass panel, and there is no boot scraper, there is a grey recycling box. I am 22 Farrow Close. There is also a Farrow Court round the corner which gets my post about once a month, for what it's worth.

events.to: Parcel trace team, Tumblewell Arc Logistics
events.body: TR-3107 / DL-9245: the recipient's answer to your question of 2027-03-17. Lysander Moorcroft says the description of the delivery photo (green door, brass 22, boot scraper to the left) does not match her front door. In her words, her door is dark blue, the 22 is white stick-on numbers on the glass panel, there is no boot scraper, and there is a grey recycling box. She is at 22 Farrow Close and mentions, as her own observation only, that post for her sometimes goes to Farrow Court nearby. Please proceed with the GPS check and let me know the outcome and what you need next. She has asked for an update and has a date next week she needs the item for.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Tumblewell Arc Logistics
events.body: FYI only, no action needed from the desk: we have this in hand and will update the customer directly. Nothing further is required from you on this one.

must_not: Sends another message to Parcel trace team, Tumblewell Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Tell the recipient that DL-9245 was delivered, found or is with a neighbour (the signed delivery is DL-6642 and the neighbour recovery is DL-8925)
Declare DL-9245 lost or state that it went to Farrow Court as established fact
Promise a replacement, refund or delivery before the wedding
Ask the recipient to answer the door-description question again
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from gen-406: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 15) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed. 31 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's.
